questions.q: What two S3 features protect northfield-raw-zone in this lesson's DR plan?
options: Object Lock and a 24-hour retention limit
Versioning (recoverable overwrites/deletes) and cross-region replication to northfield-raw-zone-dr-west in us-west-2
Intelligent-Tiering and same-region replication only
Encryption and a single nightly manual backup
questions.explain: Versioning makes accidental deletes/overwrites recoverable, and CRR copies objects to a DR bucket in a second region.

questions.q: Why is the curated zone NOT cross-region replicated in this plan?
options: The curated zone is more important than the raw zone, so it gets a different backup method entirely
It's fully reproducible by re-running northfield-orders-etl against the raw zone, so replicating it would duplicate storage cost unnecessarily
Cross-region replication is only available for CSV files
S3 does not support replication for Parquet files
questions.explain: Since curated data is a derived output reproducible from the raw zone, replicating it would be redundant cost for data that isn't the actual source of truth.

questions.q: What is the retention policy for Redshift's automated snapshots in this project, and what supplements them?
options: Automated snapshots are disabled; only manual snapshots are used
1 day retention, taken only once a month
30 days retention with no manual snapshots
7 days retention for automated snapshots, plus a manual snapshot before every schema-touching deploy
questions.explain: Automated daily snapshots are kept 7 days, and a manual snapshot is taken before any deploy that touches schema as extra insurance.

questions.q: Why does this lesson state a regional S3 outage's RPO as roughly 24 hours instead of a much smaller number?
options: Because Redshift snapshots take exactly 24 hours to restore
Because the number was chosen arbitrarily with no connection to the pipeline's design
Because AWS guarantees exactly 24-hour recovery points for all S3 replication
Because this is a nightly batch pipeline — RPO can't be better than 'since the last successful run' without adding real-time replication the project doesn't actually need
questions.explain: The guide is explicit that honest RPO numbers must match how the system actually runs — a nightly batch pipeline can't promise a sub-hour RPO without real infrastructure to back it.

questions.q: What is the stated recovery approach for a bad Redshift load or schema change?
options: Restore the last automated or manual snapshot, targeting roughly 1-2 hours RTO
Delete the Redshift workgroup and rebuild it from scratch every time
There is no recovery path defined for this scenario
Manually re-type every row of data from the raw CSVs
questions.explain: The RTO/RPO table states restoring a snapshot (automated or manual) as the recovery path, targeting 1-2 hours RTO.
